text:
Sam: Quick design riff — thinking of a small, transient 'credence' snackbar in the console when the platform auto-fallbacks. Shows why we degraded, a probation window, and a fidelity score. Want to sync on copy + telemetry hooks.
Li: Love the idea. What exactly is 'credence' here?
Sam: Short for operator credence — a 0-100 heuristic that conveys confidence in the fallback decision. Computed from weighted signals (error rate, latency spike magnitude, model mismatch score).
Nate: How is that different from 'reason code' we already surface?
Sam: Reason code stays (e.g., ERROR_502, LATENCY_HIGH). Credence is the composite confidence number + human-friendly phrase (e.g., "highly likely auto-degraded"). Makes operator triage faster.
Priya: We should include a probation window too — e.g., "probation: 5m" meaning we will sample requests back to primary model for quality checks.
Emily: +1 on probation. Also we need an audit id for every fallback event so downstream logs & eval jobs can fetch exact request samples. Suggest header `X-Fallback-ID`.
Sam: Agree. Proposal: snackbar contains: 1) short phrase (reason), 2) credence badge, 3) probation timer, 4) link to audit playback. Example UI: `FELLBACK to small-quant v2 — reason: LATENCY_HIGH — credence 82% — probation 5m — [view sample]`
Li: Nice. On telemetry: what signals into the credence calc? Can we keep it simple to start?
Sam: Minimal inputs v1: error_rate (1m), p95 latency delta, model-compatibility (binary), recent rollout traffic fraction. Weighted sum normalized to 0-100. We can evolve.
Nate: For ops, we need an escape hatch copy: "Undo fallback" + "Mark as false positive" so humans can override and trigger immediate re-eval.
Priya: If operator marks false positive, create a sampled trace bundle and attach to the audit event. TTL for traces = 30d by default, configurable per-org.
Emily: So audit event fields: fallback_id, primary_model, fallback_model, reason_code, credence_score, probation_until, sample_links. And we should store a compact telemetry signature for privacy-preserving search.
Sam: Agree. For search we can store a fingerprint string (sha256 of normalized metadata) rather than full payload. That lets us find likely correlated events without exposing raw inputs.
Li: UX question: snackbar lifespan — do we make it persistent until resolved or auto-dismiss after probation?
Nate: Prefer persistent pin in console for probation window, then auto-dismiss but keep entry in "Fallback History" with quick replay.
Priya: Also add a mode toggle per-team: "auto-fallback probation = enable/disable" and default to enabled for non-prod orgs.
Sam: Good. Small config proto (console):
```json
{
  "auto_fallback": true,
  "probation_window_seconds": 300,
  "credence_threshold": 60,
  "sample_retention_days": 30,
  "export_header_name": "X-Fallback-ID"
}
```
Emily: Nice. For API: we should emit an event to our telemetry pipeline: `fallback.event` with fallback_id and compact metrics. Also surface the fallback_id in request logs so SREs can correlate.
deploy-bot: canary rollout v0.1 of snackbar prototype => env=staging, rollout=5% :rocket:
Li: One risk: cluttering product teams with too many false positives. We must tune credence to bias towards precision for initial launch.
Sam: Agreed — default credence_threshold=60 means only show snackbar when reasonably confident. We'll provide a "verbose" mode for early adopters.
Nate: Action items: 1) Nate to mock snackbar UI + copy, 2) Emily to draft telemetry schema and fallback_id header, 3) Priya to wire probation/trace retention policy, 4) Sam to write short engineer-facing spec.
Priya: I'll also add a small Playbook blurb: what to do when credence > 80% vs 60-80%.
Li: Can we hold a 20m sync tomorrow? I'll invite SRE + support.
Sam: Sounds good. Thanks all. :+1:
